Elevated C-Reactive Protein (CRP) in Hemodialysis Patients With Moderate/Severe Uremic Pruritus: A Potential Mediator of High Overall Mortality. BACKGROUND
The main takeaway from our work is that

the elevated CRP levels in hemodialysis (HD) patients with moderate or severe pruritus (MP or SP) may be a marker of the underlying systemic inflammatory state that contributes to their increased mortality risk, and that this may be an additional mechanism by which pruritus is a predictor of mortality in HD patients.
the elevated CRP levels in patients with uremic pruritis are not only an indicator of inflammation, but may also be the cause of the high mortality rates in these patients.

the presence of moderate to severe pruritus is a strong predictor for all-cause mortality in HD patients, and that the elevated CRP level in HD patients is a strong predictor of the presence of moderate/severe pruritus.
